title: Weekday lunch on the ground floor: food hall and market (proposed fit-out)
question: Where does lunchtime foot traffic concentrate on the ground floor, which counters build the longest lines, and which change helps most?
context: Weekday lunch on the ground floor of an office building. North unit: a food hall with four food counters, a coffee bar and tables. South unit: a market with a deli, bakery, pharmacy and parcel desk. The units connect only outside, along the storefront. Office workers come down two staircases.
leaveLabel: Leave (go back upstairs or out to the street)

assumptions.why: Middle case from CoStar data: about 29 office workers from upstairs, plus 10% of the workers and 3% of the households that the CoStar kit records within 500 m, plus couriers. The kit only covers some buildings, so those pools are lower bounds; the capture shares are assumptions. Low case 153, busy-day case 503.
Office workers, lunch crowd, market shoppers, couriers: the middle-case counts divided by 312. The courier share is a guess.

Upstairs floor area from Matterport divided by 240 SF per employee, the median across about 1,800 current Los Angeles office tenancies in the CoStar kit. Range 29 to 78. About 29 come down at lunch (80% present, 70% of those come down; both assumed).

The building is an empty shell. Every counter, table area, desk and restroom is a proposed fit-out placed by Claude inside the real walls. The mix (small food counters, coffee, bakery, a small market, parcel pickup, an optical counter) follows what occupies storefront space nearby in the CoStar kit and this building's own past tenants.
Counter-service assumptions: 30 to 60 orders an hour per counter, with the noodle bar deliberately the slowest. Not measured.
The building has very little parking for its size, so few arrive by car; the back door from the lot gets a low weight.
A relaxed indoor walking pace, about 1.25 m per second.
Nothing yet makes people buy food before sitting at the tables. Known limit.

Moved 2.1 m from (-4.95, -1.24), which sat in a notch of the staircase that the Matterport mesh shows there (swarm fitout --mesh). The gate is now at the foot of the stairs, at least 0.4 m from the staircase and the walls.

Each simulated person copies one cast member and keeps their own state, so a small cast turns one person's errand into a crowd. Each large group has 9 or more varied people, and rare errands carry a low weight.
